action.message: Always attach the original context, concrete options, and recommended default when deferring any decision item to a review backlog — a deferred item without its decision frame is an incomplete handoff.

Always require a liveness proof (heartbeat, resource-holder check, or round-trip ack) before blocking on any cross-agent dependency — an assumption of availability is a silent deadlock waiting to fire.

Always include the derivation chain (sources checked, files read, prior context) alongside any outcome report — a result without provenance is an implicit follow-up question the user hasn't asked yet.
Always identify whether a correction targets an instance or a generator; when correcting an instance, name the generator and either fix it too or explicitly note it as still active.

Always enumerate all current consumers of a shared resource before modifying or exclusively claiming it, whether the resource is a UI component, a browser session, or a codebase region with parallel workers.

Always verify an outcome at the consumer's end — the running app, the receiving agent, the user's original spec, the actual output rows — never at the producer's end where success is structurally guaranteed.

Before declaring a multi-dimensional feature complete, enumerate all axes of the domain (filter criteria, data sources, visual modes, page instances) and verify coverage across each — feature-structural completeness is not domain-structural completeness.
Always match the output weight to the question weight — a direct question gets a direct sentence, a simple list gets markdown, and HTML is reserved for genuinely interactive or multi-state content.

Always proceed without pausing on execution-level continuation signals, and always halt on product-level behavioral decisions — never invert this by pausing on execution while silently resolving product scope.
